questions.question: Tell me about your experience and why this role interests you.
questions.tip: Choose two or three relevant facts. Experience from work, study, volunteering or a personal project can be useful.

questions.question: Tell me about a problem you helped solve. What did you personally do?
questions.tip: Use Situation, Task, Action and Result. Keep the result factual; a number is useful only when you can support it.

questions.question: Describe a time you worked with another person to complete a task.
questions.tip: Explain your contribution, how you communicated and what you learned about working together.

questions.question: How did you learn something new that you needed for a task?
questions.tip: Describe the starting gap, the steps you took and something you can now demonstrate.

questions.question: How do you check that your work is accurate or complete?
questions.tip: Give one concrete example of a check. Explain what you do when you find an error.

questions.question: Tell me about useful feedback you received and what you changed.
questions.tip: Focus on the feedback, your response and the next attempt. You do not need to share private personal circumstances.

questions.question: Which part of this role would you need to develop, and how would you start?
questions.tip: Name an honest gap and a manageable first action. Do not claim a skill you have not yet practised.

questions.question: What would you like to ask us about the role or team?
questions.tip: Ask about responsibilities, support, expectations or a requirement that is unclear in the advert.
